subtype: Approach: report threats to the cybercrime cell and the college [Action]
passage:
Sachin scrolled through the comments on the bus from the town college, and his stomach went cold. One gave the name of his lane. Another said they knew which house was his and might visit. The rest were insults he could no longer laugh off.

He did not answer a single one. Instead he took screenshots, closed the app, and went straight to Pooja madam, his lecturer, and put the phone in front of her. She read the comments, and her jaw tightened. "This is not something you fight online, Sachin."

That afternoon in the computer room she sat next to him while he filed a complaint on the cybercrime portal, and then walked him to the principal, who rang his father.

qa.q: What did one comment give away about Sachin?
qa.a: It gave the name of his lane.

qa.q: What was Sachin feeling on the bus when he read the comments?
qa.a: Sachin felt scared and shaken, shown by his stomach going cold and the insults he could no longer laugh off.

qa.q: What could Sachin do besides reporting while the complaint is looked into, and why?
qa.a: Sachin could stay near family or a friend and share the saved screenshots with them, because his safety matters more than any online fight.

qa.q: How might Sachin's father feel when the principal rings him?
qa.a: Sachin's father may be alarmed and protective, though grateful that the college acted the same day to keep his son safe.

grounding: When comments include threats and the home address, the student files a complaint on the cybercrime portal and informs the college authorities.

subtype: Approach: report threats to the cybercrime cell and the college [Action]
passage:
Lindiwe's post criticising a Johannesburg student society's fee rise had drawn hundreds of replies. Most were rude. Then one arrived that listed the name of her street and said, "We know where to find you."
Her flatmate Xin read it over her shoulder and went pale. "That's not an argument any more."
Lindiwe did not reply. She screenshotted the comment and two others with her address, noted the dates and usernames, and opened the police service's online reporting page. She filled in the complaint, attached the images and got a reference number. Then she emailed the university's student safety office with the same screenshots.
The safety office phoned within the hour. An officer asked if she felt safe at home, arranged for campus security to walk her between lectures, and said they would contact the society about the posts.
That night she left her phone in the kitchen and did not look at the thread.

qa.q: What did the threatening comment list?
qa.a: It listed the name of her street and said they knew where to find her.

qa.q: How did Xin react to the comment, and what does it suggest Xin felt?
qa.a: Xin went pale and said it was no longer an argument, suggesting fear and alarm at seeing Lindiwe's street named.

qa.q: Why was reporting a better choice than replying online?
qa.a: A reply could provoke the person further, while the police report and the safety office's response actually protect Lindiwe.

qa.q: How did the safety office respond?
qa.a: It phoned within the hour, checked if she felt safe, arranged campus security to walk her between lectures and said it would contact the society.

grounding: Shows a student facing threats that include their address and reporting them to the police and university authorities instead of fighting online.

subtype: Approach: report threats to the cybercrime cell and the college [Action]
passage:
The college administration block smelled of old files. Nilesh sat across from Professor Uma, the dean of students, with his laptop open.
"This one has my home address," he said, turning the screen. "And this says my younger brother's school. I filed a complaint on the national cybercrime portal last night. Here's the acknowledgement number."
Professor Uma read each screenshot slowly. "You did right not to answer them. Did you tell your family?"
"My mother knows. She's the one who told me to come here first thing."
Professor Uma picked up the phone and called the college's grievance cell and the security head while he waited. She wrote the complaint number in her register. "Security will be at the gate for you and your brother's school will be told today. I'll email the cybercrime cell our letter this afternoon."
Nilesh let out a long breath and closed the laptop.

qa.q: Where did Nilesh file the complaint the night before?
qa.a: He filed it on the national cybercrime portal.

qa.q: What does Nilesh's long breath at the end suggest?
qa.a: It suggests he felt relieved, after carrying the fear alone, once the dean took clear steps the same day.

qa.q: What else could Nilesh do to keep his case strong?
qa.a: He could keep saving any new threats with dates and hand them to the college and the cybercrime cell, rather than replying to them.

qa.q: How does Professor Uma see her role here?
qa.a: She treats the threats as serious, calling the grievance cell and security at once and arranging protection for Nilesh and his brother.

grounding: Shows a student reporting online threats that include a home address to the cybercrime portal and the college, and the college acting the same day.
